title: Value
description: A motivation element stating the worth, benefit, or utility that a specific concept, service, feature, or outcome has for one or more named stakeholders, expressed from the stakeholder's perspective (for example 'saves customers ten minutes per order') rather than as a target, a result, or a need. Use Outcome instead when the statement describes an end result the organization intends or has achieved, such as a measurable state change, rather than why that result is worth something to a stakeholder. Use Goal instead when the statement expresses a desired direction or end state the organization strives toward, not the benefit a stakeholder derives. Use Meaning instead when the statement gives the interpretation or definition of a concept in a context, not its worth or importance. Use Driver instead when the statement describes a condition or force that motivates change, such as market pressure or regulation, rather than a benefit delivered.

documentation.description: Free-text explanation of the value: which stakeholders it applies to, what benefit they gain, and any quantification or evidence. Set it whenever the element name alone does not state who benefits and how.

valueType.description: Category of worth or utility this value represents

x-dr-evidence: A 'Value proposition', 'Benefits' or 'Why this matters' section in a product spec, PRD or README that names a stakeholder and the benefit they receive
A business case, OKR or ADR 'Consequences/Benefits' entry quantifying worth to a stakeholder, such as cost saved, revenue enabled or time reduced
A feature, epic or service catalogue entry with a 'value', 'benefit' or 'business value' field describing what a user or customer gains
